draft.title: Values in business decisions
card: Values are the beliefs a person thinks are important, such as honesty and fairness. An entrepreneur's values can shape the choices they make in their business.
Honesty
An entrepreneur who values honesty tells customers the truth about what they sell, including any faults or limits.
Fairness
An entrepreneur who values fairness pays workers properly and treats them with respect.
Law
An entrepreneur who values following the law keeps to the rules that apply to a business, such as safety and pay rules.
draft.remember: What an entrepreneur believes is important can guide the choices they make in business.

a.q: Which choice shows an entrepreneur acting on the value of honesty?
opts: Telling customers about a fault in a second-hand bike
Paying every worker on time each fortnight
Getting a licence before opening a food van
Lowering a price to match a nearby shop
a.why: Telling customers the truth about a fault shows honesty. Paying workers on time shows fairness, and getting a licence shows following the law. Matching a price is a choice about competing, not a value shown here.
a.clue: Which choice is about telling the truth to customers?

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Hobart. A new worker is not yet trained on the oven, and a busy shift is coming. Priya trains the worker first, and does not skip the safety rules to save time. Which value is she mainly acting on?
opts: Following the law, and caring for her worker
Honesty, because she is telling customers the truth
Making the most profit from the busy shift
Being the first bakery in Hobart to open early
b.why: Priya keeps to safety rules and looks after her worker, so she is acting on following the law and treating workers well. Honesty with customers is not part of the case. Skipping safety to save time would be the opposite of her choice.
b.clue: Think about who the choice protects: a worker, not a customer.

a.best: Telling customers about a fault in a second-hand bike

b.best: Following the law, and caring for her worker
